title: Epic: OrcaSlicer Profile Customization - Full Settings Editors
description:
## Overview
Enable full OrcaSlicer-style profile editing for Machine, Filament, and Process profiles. Users can override any setting and save as custom profiles with full flattened JSON storage.

## Goals
1. Complete Process Profile Editor - Expand existing SlicerSettingsPanel with all OrcaSlicer settings
2. Create Filament Profile Editor - Temperature, cooling, retraction, flow settings matching OrcaSlicer UI
3. Create Machine Profile Editor - Build volume, G-code, extruder settings matching OrcaSlicer UI
4. Change Tracking System - Highlight modified settings with reset-to-original capability
5. Tab Dirty Indicators - Visual feedback when a category tab contains modified settings

## Design Decisions
- Edit workflow: Edit in modal then Save as Custom prompt (OrcaSlicer style)
- Profile storage: Full flattened JSON (no inheritance/delta)
- Extruder support: Single extruder only

## Reference UI
- Filament: Basic info, Flow ratio, Pressure advance, Chamber temp, Print temp, Bed temp, Volumetric, Cooling
- Machine: Printable space, G-code flavor, Thumbnails, Cooling fan, Extruder clearance, Adaptive bed mesh, Machine G-code
- Process: Quality (layer/line/seam), Strength (infill/walls), Speed, Support, Acceleration, Retraction, Cooling, Advanced
close_reason: All profile editors implemented and integrated - Machine, Filament, Process with full OrcaSlicer-style settings, change tracking, and tab dirty indicators

title: Add change tracking system with useTrackedSettings hook
description:
## Summary
Create a React hook and utilities to track original vs current values for profile settings, enabling reset-to-original functionality and dirty state detection per category.

## Implementation

### 1. Create useTrackedSettings<T> hook in slicerSettingsTypes.ts
- Interface TrackedState<T> with original, current, hasChanges, getChangedKeys, resetToOriginal, resetAll, isDirty, changedKeysPerCategory
- Hook stores deep copy of initial settings as original
- Returns functions for change detection and reset

### 2. Category mapping for dirty indicators
Map each setting key to its category tab (Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Other) so tabs can show dirty state.

### 3. Deep equality check
Use deep comparison for nested objects/arrays to accurately detect changes.

## Files to Modify
- src/Web/ReactApp/src/features/slicer/components/settings/slicerSettingsTypes.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] useTrackedSettings hook created with full TypeScript typing
- [ ] hasChanges(key) returns true only when current differs from original
- [ ] resetToOriginal(key) restores single setting to original value
- [ ] changedKeysPerCategory correctly groups changed settings by tab
- [ ] isDirty is true when any setting has changed

- Pencil icon button next to Filament Profile dropdown

### 2. Create ProfileEditorModal component

  - Renders appropriate editor component
  - Has 'Save as Custom Profile' and 'Cancel' buttons
  - Warns on close if unsaved changes (via isDirty)

- Parse rawJson if available, or use settings object
- Pre-populate editor with profile values
- Store original for change tracking

### 4. Save as Custom Profile flow
- When 'Save as Custom' clicked:
  - Prompt for custom profile name (default: 'Copy of {original}')
  - Flatten all settings to full JSON (no inheritance)
  - Call POST /api/slicer/profiles/upload with:
    - rawJson: JSON.stringify(flattenedSettings)
    - profileType: 'machine' | 'filament' | 'process'
    - name: user-provided name
  - Close modal
  - Refresh profile list
  - Auto-select new custom profile

### 5. Unsaved changes warning
- If isDirty and user tries to close modal, show confirmation

title: Epic: OrcaSlicer Profile Selection Flow Redesign
description:
## Overview
The slicer panel profile selection flow is fundamentally broken. The current implementation uses printer instances instead of printer models, hardcodes filament profiles, and shows worker versions instead of slicer types.

## Required Flow (OrcaSlicer-style)
1. **Printer Model** → User selects from catalog (/api/catalog/printer-models)
2. **Machine Profiles** → Populated based on selected printer model (with nozzle variants)
3. **Filament Profiles** → Filtered by selected machine profile (from API, not hardcoded)
4. **Process Profiles** → Filtered by selected machine profile (from API)
5. **Slicer Selection** → Shows slicer types/versions (OrcaSlicer, PrusaSlicer), not worker info

## Current Problems
| Component | Current | Required |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| Printer Selection | selectedPrinterId (instances) | Printer Model from catalog |
| Machine Profiles | Not shown, flat list | Dropdown filtered by printer model |
| Filament Profiles | Hardcoded MATERIAL_PRESETS | API-driven, filtered by machine |
| Process Profiles | Returns ALL profiles | Filtered by machine profile |
| Slicer Selection | Worker versions | Slicer types/versions |

## API Support Available
- /api/catalog/printer-models - printer models with specs
- /api/slicer/profiles/hierarchy?machineProfileId=X - filtered profiles
- byHierarchy[manufacturer].models[model] structure exists

## Files to Modify
- src/Web/ReactApp/src/features/slicer/pages/NewSliceJobPage.tsx
- src/Web/ReactApp/src/services/slicerProfilesService.ts
- Possibly: src/Web/ReactApp/src/features/slicer/components/ProfileSelector.tsx

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Profile selection cascades: Model → Machine → Filament/Process
- [ ] No hardcoded material presets
- [ ] Slicer dropdown shows types, not worker info
- [ ] All profiles come from API
- [ ] UI matches OrcaSlicer-style workflow
close_reason: Epic completed: All 16 sub-tasks finished. Profile selection flow redesigned with cascading model→machine→filament/process selection, API-driven profiles, custom profile management, comprehensive unit tests, and component refactoring.

title: Implement hybrid slicer profile architecture: OrcaSlicer worker + PostgreSQL
description:
## Architectural Decision

Implement a **hybrid approach** for slicer profile management:

1. **System Profiles** → Served directly by OrcaSlicer worker (read-only)
   - 3000+ filament profiles, 2000+ process profiles from OrcaSlicer disk files
   - Queried incrementally from OrcaSlicer worker API
   - Single source of truth for manufacturer/OrcaFilamentLibrary profiles
   - No duplication in PostgreSQL

2. **Custom Profiles** → Stored in PostgreSQL
   - User-created profiles (new from scratch)
   - User-modified profiles (cloned from system, then customized)
   - User-uploaded profiles (e.g., Micron 180 with no OrcaSlicer support)
   - Marked with `isSystem=false`

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Incremental System Profile Loading (NewSliceJobPage)
- Remove `listHierarchical()` query that loads ALL profiles upfront
- Add incremental queries to OrcaSlicer worker:
  1. User selects printer → `GET /api/profiles/machine/{printerModel}`
  2. User selects machine profile → `POST /api/profiles/filament/for-machines`
  3. Same for process → `POST /api/profiles/process/for-machines`
- Add service methods to `slicerProfilesService.ts` for new endpoints

### Phase 2: Custom Profile Management
- Keep PostgreSQL tables for custom profiles only
- Add `cloneProfile` endpoint to create custom copy from system profile
- Add `uploadProfile` endpoint for user uploads
- UI shows merged view: system profiles (from worker) + custom profiles (from DB)

### Phase 3: Cleanup
- Remove system profile seeding from PostgreSQL (no longer needed)
- Remove duplicate profile data from database
- Update SlicerProfilesPage to use hybrid approach

## API Endpoints

**OrcaSlicer Worker (system profiles):**
- `GET /api/profiles/machine/{printerModel}` - Machine profiles for model
- `POST /api/profiles/filament/for-machines` - Filament for machines
- `POST /api/profiles/process/for-machines` - Process for machines
- `GET /api/profiles/filament/templates` - OrcaFilamentLibrary universals

**API Server (custom profiles):**
- `GET /api/slicer/profiles/custom` - User's custom profiles
- `POST /api/slicer/profiles/clone` - Clone system profile to custom
- `POST /api/slicer/profiles/upload` - Upload custom profile

## Files to Modify

- `src/Web/ReactApp/src/services/slicerProfilesService.ts` - Add incremental methods
- `src/Web/ReactApp/src/features/slicer/pages/NewSliceJobPage.tsx` - Use incremental queries
- `src/api/Services/Slicing/ProfilesService.cs` - Custom profile management
- `src/api/Controllers/Slicing/ProfilesController.cs` - Clone/upload endpoints

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] System profiles queried incrementally from OrcaSlicer worker
- [ ] Custom profiles stored in PostgreSQL with isSystem=false
- [ ] Clone workflow: system profile → custom copy in DB
- [ ] Upload workflow: user file → custom profile in DB
- [ ] UI merges both sources for profile selection
- [ ] No duplicate system profiles in PostgreSQL

title: Phase 1: Incremental system profile loading from OrcaSlicer worker
description:
## Goal

Replace the upfront loading of ALL profiles with incremental queries to OrcaSlicer worker based on user selections.

## Current Problem

```typescript
// Loads EVERYTHING upfront (3000+ filament, 2000+ process profiles)
const { data: hierarchyProfiles } = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['slicerProfilesHierarchy'],
  queryFn: () => slicerProfilesService.listHierarchical(),
});
```

## Required Flow

1. User selects printer → Query machine profiles for that model
2. User selects machine profile → Query filament + process profiles for that machine

## Implementation

### 1. Add service methods to slicerProfilesService.ts

```typescript
// Query OrcaSlicer worker directly (not API server)
const ORCA_WORKER_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_ORCA_WORKER_URL || 'http://localhost:8080';

async getMachineProfilesForModel(printerModel: string): Promise<MachineProfileListItem[]>
```

title: Phase 2: Custom profile management (clone/upload to PostgreSQL)
description:
## Goal

Implement custom profile management where users can clone system profiles or upload their own.

## Use Cases

1. **Clone & Customize**: User takes a system profile (e.g., 'Generic ABS @Ratrig') and modifies settings
2. **Upload Own**: User has a printer with no OrcaSlicer profiles (e.g., Micron 180) and uploads their own
3. **Create New**: User creates a profile from scratch

## Implementation

### 1. API Endpoints (ProfilesController.cs)

```csharp
// Clone a system profile to create a custom copy
POST /api/slicer/profiles/clone
Body: { sourceProfileId: string, sourceType: 'machine'|'filament'|'process', name: string }
Returns: CustomProfileDto

// Upload a custom profile
POST /api/slicer/profiles/upload
Body: { rawJson: string, profileType: 'machine'|'filament'|'process', name: string }
Returns: CustomProfileDto

// List user's custom profiles
GET /api/slicer/profiles/custom
Returns: CustomProfileDto[]

// Update custom profile
PUT /api/slicer/profiles/custom/{id}
Body: { rawJson: string, name: string }

// Delete custom profile
DELETE /api/slicer/profiles/custom/{id}
```

### 2. Database Schema

Custom profiles stored in existing tables with `isSystem=false`:
- ProcessProfile
- FilamentProfile (may need to add)
- MachineProfile

### 3. Frontend Service Methods

```typescript
async cloneProfile(sourceId: string, sourceType: string, name: string): Promise<CustomProfile>
async uploadProfile(rawJson: string, profileType: string, name: string): Promise<CustomProfile>
async listCustomProfiles(): Promise<CustomProfile[]>
async updateCustomProfile(id: string, data: Partial<CustomProfile>): Promise<CustomProfile>
async deleteCustomProfile(id: string): Promise<void>
```

### 4. UI Integration

- Add 'Clone' button on system profile hover/selection
- Add 'Upload Profile' button in profile management
- Show custom profiles merged with system profiles in selectors
- Visual indicator for custom vs system profiles

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Clone endpoint creates custom copy from system profile
- [ ] Upload endpoint accepts raw JSON profile
- [ ] Custom profiles stored with isSystem=false
- [ ] UI shows merged view of system + custom profiles
- [ ] User can edit/delete their custom profiles
- [ ] System profiles remain read-only

title: Phase 3: Cleanup - Remove system profile duplication from PostgreSQL
description:

## Implementation

### 1. Remove Profile Seeding

### 2. Update SlicerProfilesPage

- Custom profiles from PostgreSQL

### 3. Database Cleanup

- Keep custom profiles (where isSystem=false)
- May need migration script

### 4. Update API ProfilesService

- System profiles handled by OrcaSlicer worker queries

```typescript
const { data: hierarchyProfiles } = useQuery({
```

title: Multi-Print Job Tracking (Print Projects)
description:
Enable print farm operators to manage print jobs that span multiple prints/plates. Operators often need to fulfill requests requiring multiple gcode files (e.g., all parts for a Voron 2.4). This feature allows grouping multiple gcode files into a 'Project' and tracking which files have been printed vs remaining to complete the entire project.

## Use Case
- Operator receives request to print all parts for a printer kit (e.g., Voron 2.4)
- Multiple plates are sliced to gcode (some in base color, some in accent color)
- Operator uploads all plates to PrintFarmer
- Operator creates a 'Project' grouping all related gcode files
- System tracks print completion status for each file
- Dashboard shows overall project progress

## Key Features
- Create/manage Print Projects
- Associate gcode files with projects
- Track completion status per file
- Support for color/material requirements per file
- Project progress dashboard
- Project templates for common printer kits

title: Automatic print completion tracking via SignalR
description:
Integrate print completion events with project tracking.

## Features
- When a print completes on a printer, automatically update project file status
- SignalR notifications when project files are marked complete
- Real-time progress updates on project detail page
- Toast notifications for project milestones (50%, 100% complete)

## Implementation
- Listen to printer job completion events
- Match completed print to project files
- Update PrintProjectFile.PrintedCount
- Broadcast SignalR event for project progress update
- Update project status when all files complete

## Considerations
- Handle prints started outside of PrintFarmer
- Support manual marking as complete
- Handle re-printing (multiple copies)
- Track which printer completed each file
close_reason: Implemented using React Query auto-refresh (30s interval). Full SignalR integration deferred for simpler approach.
